findings:
🟠 [flock-missing-fallback] MUST-FIX The foreman-required missing-flock path is absent: `hooks/tests/run.sh` gates only on `AUTOPILOT_TEST_SNAPSHOT=0` and `command -v rsync`, there is no `test-snapshot: disabled (flock missing)` line, and no test hides flock from PATH. Impact: on a host without flock the outer run enters snapshot mode and cannot take the G5 live lock, instead of running in place under the guard. Smallest remediation: add `elif ! command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "test-snapshot: disabled (flock missing)" >&2; __ts_inplace_wrap` beside the rsync branch, add a real outer fixture case with a PATH that lacks flock asserting that line, the in-place run and the guard still firing, and name flock in the README opt-out sentence.
🟡 [oracle-lock-ppid-bypass] MUST-FIX The new `ps -o args= -p "$PPID"` branch in `hooks/tests/run.sh` runs a full suite in place whenever the parent command line contains `suite-oracle-lock.test.sh`, and prints no `test-snapshot: disabled` line. Impact: G3 allows an in-place full run only with that one stderr line, so this is a silent, undocumented third opt-out keyed on a spoofable substring. Smallest remediation: print `test-snapshot: disabled (suite-oracle-lock parent)` to stderr in that branch before `__ts_inplace_wrap` and list it with the other opt-outs in the README paragraph.
🔵 [exit-cleanup-signal-mask] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `trap '' INT TERM` and `TS_SHUTDOWN_STARTED` are set only inside `__ts_outer_on_interrupt`. If `__suite_on_exit` (body not in this diff) does not mask INT/TERM itself, a signal during normal-path cleanup calls `exit` inside the EXIT trap and skips the remaining guard/remove steps. Excluded because it cannot be confirmed from the diff; if confirmed, set the mask and flag at the top of the EXIT handler.
🔵 [worktree-reap-unproven] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The diff adds no worktree reaping to the outer shutdown path, and both worktree tests (and the reaper free-lock test) place the worktree inside the container, so a plain `rm -rf` satisfies them. Excluded because the tests meet the brief's literal wording and `ts_snapshot_remove` from P4a may already reap; a worktree outside the container would pin the "from inside repo first" step.
🔵 [no-setsid-fallback-pgroup] CUT/FOLLOW-UP After the switch from `set -m` to `set +m`, the last fallback (`exec bash` with neither setsid nor python3) no longer gives the child its own process group, so group signalling and `ts_wait_pgid_gone` do nothing there. Excluded because Linux always ships setsid and hosts without it also lack flock, which goes in place once the flock gate exists.
🔵 [nonzero-child-case] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The appended section has no dedicated "exit path non-zero child" case with the private-TMPDIR residue assertion; the inversion case fails through the guard, not the child. Excluded because P4a's existing outer-run tests are stated to cover non-zero exits.
🔵 [test-hygiene] CUT/FOLLOW-UP Non-blocking test nits: the TERM-mid-construction rsync shim hardcodes `/usr/bin/rsync` and always costs about 20s because bash defers the trap until the shim returns. The reaper live-lock cases kill `flock` but leave its `sleep 30` child holding the lock. `ts_wait_pgid_gone` carries a dead `if [ "$n" -eq 0 ]` block.
